claims.text: In a single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloy, thermal conductivity has a non-monotonic dependence on the degree of chemical short-range order.
Thermal conductivity reaches a distinct minimum before SRO clusters percolate.
Percolation of SRO clusters causes a sharp increase in thermal conductivity beyond standard phonon-scattering-model predictions.
The conductivity upturn is driven by a coherent, low-scattering pathway for high-frequency phonons.
Controlled annealing or molecular-dynamics quenching can tune SRO from a random state to isolated clusters and then to a percolating network while retaining the bcc phase.
The proposed operating range is 0.5 Tm to 0.8 Tm.
Anharmonicity is significant in the proposed high-temperature operating range.
The alloy remains a thermodynamically stable, single-phase bcc solid solution without phase separation under the proposed conditions.
The structural mediator is a continuous network of chemically ordered clusters, potentially including Nb-Ta-rich or Hf-Zr-rich domains.
At low SRO, mass variance and local strain fields increase phonon scattering and reduce thermal conductivity.
Growth and percolation of ordered clusters reduce local potential-energy fluctuations along the connected path.
Reduced potential-energy fluctuations along the connected path lower the scattering rates of high-frequency phonons.
In the percolating state, thermal conductivity becomes higher than that of the random solid solution at the same temperature.
The predicted percolative conductivity enhancement violates predictions based on Matthiessen's rule and independent point-defect scattering.
The proposed effect does not apply when SRO causes phase separation or when ordered clusters remain isolated.
The proposed effect is most pronounced for high-frequency phonons.
Existing interatomic potentials may not accurately capture the energetic driving force for SRO in HfNbTaTiZr-like complex alloys.
A machine-learned interatomic potential should be trained on DFT configurations for the specific HfNbTaTiZr system to represent its potential-energy surface and SRO evolution.
Comparing random, isolated-cluster, and percolating-cluster states using Green-Kubo conductivity, SRO metrics, and cluster analysis can distinguish a percolative transition from simple scattering.
The hypothesis is falsified if conductivity does not rise above the random-solid-solution value at percolation.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome already expects an initial monotonic decrease before the percolative upturn, but the falsification rule says that a monotonic decrease 'up to the percolation threshold' is itself sufficient to falsify the hypothesis. A decrease up to that threshold is compatible with the prediction unless behavior at or beyond the threshold is also specified.
